reference: GNU coreutils nl selected from the harness reference PATH. Each parity fixture runs as the same Bash script against GNU nl and the compiled-in nl builtin; byte output, exit status and resulting fixture tree are compared under the harness C locale and UTC.
coverage: Default nonempty-line numbering, blank lines, and an unterminated final record.
All-line numbering with starting value, increment, zero-padded field, width, and custom separator.
Default logical-page sections with section-specific styles and reset, plus a custom delimiter with no-reset numbering.
BRE-based body selection using anchors and an interval.
Documented long aliases after an operand.
Numbering carried across named files and stdin selected by the '-' operand.
BRE matching over a record containing NUL.
Missing-file diagnostics while later operands continue, and invalid BRE failure.
Bash builtin type and help metadata contract.
exclusions: PTY streaming before stdin reaches EOF is deferred because this fixture runner has no PTY driver.
No privileged, hardware, network, or host-system operation is part of nl's text-numbering contract.
Broad libc regex locale behavior, extreme line sizes, write failures, and exhaustive option/error matrices remain outside this compact suite.
The case count exceeds the preferred range to preserve existing cases and isolate additional boundaries and regressions.

cases.purpose: Check default nonempty-line numbering, preserved blank records, and GNU nl's newline on an unterminated final record.
Check numbering every record with a nondefault start and increment, zero padding, field width, and a literal separator.
Check -l grouping over multiple blank runs, including a trailing single blank, with left alignment.
Check default page delimiters, distinct header/body/footer styles, reset numbering, a multi-character custom delimiter, and -p continuation.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '\:\:\:' 'H1' 'H2' '\:\:' 'B1' '' 'B2' '\:' 'F1' 'F2' > pages
nl -h a -b t -f a -v 4 -i 2 -w 2 pages
printf '%s\n' '@@@@@@' 'head' '@@@@' 'body' '@@' 'tail' > custom
nl -ba -d '@@' -v 8 -p -w 2 custom

cases.purpose: Check POSIX basic regular-expression selection with anchors and an escaped interval; unmatched lines retain the number field.
Check documented long aliases, equals-form arguments, and option permutation after a file operand.
Check that a single invocation carries its line counter from a named file through stdin via '-' and into a later named file.
cases.script:
printf 'left
' > first
printf 'right
' > last
printf 'middle
' | nl -ba first - last

cases.purpose: Check GNU BRE matching after an embedded NUL while preserving the record bytes in output.
Check the GNU error status and diagnostic for a missing operand while valid files on either side are still processed.
cases.script:
printf 'before\n' > before
printf 'after\n' > after
nl -ba before absent after

cases.purpose: Check failure on a malformed basic regular expression.
Check Bash's builtin type and documented help topic against the nl source documentation.
cases.script:
type -t nl
doc=$(help nl)
[[ $doc == *"Number lines (POSIX nl)."* ]]
[[ $doc == *"--body-numbering"* ]]
printf 'help-topic-present\n'

cases.purpose: Verify that a numbered line reaches a terminal while the input side remains open.
Repeated invocations reset numbering and stdin state; calls sharing an exhausted descriptor do not reread data.
cases.script:
printf 'a\nb\n' > input
nl -ba -v 7 < input
nl -ba < input
{ nl -ba; nl -ba; } < input

cases.purpose: Empty input emits nothing; zero-padding places the sign before negative line numbers.
cases.script:
: > empty
nl empty
printf 'a\nb\n' | nl -ba -v -2 -i 1 -n rz -w 4 -s ':'
